minutes.headline: Committee heard first FY15 budget requests, approved a hockey trip, and chose a union negotiating team.
minutes.summary: The meeting recognized the 2013 superintendent scholar and covered a heating leak with asbestos at the high school, the PARCC pilot tests, and the Middle High School project update ahead of January votes. It opened FY15 budget season with nursing and special education presentations, accepted donations, approved a hockey trip, and set a negotiating team. It ended in executive session on paraprofessional bargaining.

public_comment.topic: PTO voted unanimously to support the Middle High School building project.

what_happened.line: The committee opened FY15 budget season with requests from nursing (a physician line increase) and special education (increases across several lines).
The committee accepted donations from the police relief association and a Target program; the vote was not audible in the captions.
The committee approved the ice hockey trip to Waterville Valley; the vote was not audible in the captions.
A member and the superintendent will serve on the team negotiating the contract that expires June 30.
The building project update reported a reduced design contingency, taken from the local share, ahead of January votes on the Middle High School project.

why_it_matters: The FY15 requests for special education, out-of-district tuition and nursing are the first figures that will shape next year's school budget and, through it, the town budget, mostly taxes.
The Middle High School project is headed to votes in January, and the local share of its cost is what residents will be asked to approve.

The January votes on the Middle High School building project.
